page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.7xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 32 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression. However, the instance leverages its 32 dedicated cores to achieve average multi-core performance across several workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation with Clang all perform in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with read-only large block speeds at 87.55 GB/sec and write speeds at 43.49 GB/sec, though Passmark memory scores remain in the lower 25% bracket.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2.7xlarge offers a balanced resource density for multi-threaded workloads that do not require high single-core frequency or local NVMe storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention, making it suitable for parallel processing tasks. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded applications such as software compilation and medium-sized language model inference prompt processing, where its multi-core capabilities can be fully utilized.
